chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal. He said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:

God, Mighty and Majestic, does not accept an action except with recognition (ma'rifa), nor does He accept recognition except with action. So whoever recognizes, his recognition will guide him to action. And whoever does not act, he has no recognition. Verily, part of faith is from its other part.

key_terms.الإيمان بعضه من بعض: Part of faith is from another part — indicating the holistic, integrated nature of faith
key_terms.معرفة: Ma'rifa — recognition, gnosis, deep knowing; in Shia theology refers to knowing God through the Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the relationship between ma'rifa (recognition) and action in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) teaches the inseparable unity of ma'rifa (recognition/gnosis of God and the Imam) and 'amal (righteous action). This hadith reflects the Shia theological position that true knowledge of God and the Imams is not mere intellectual assent but must be embodied in practice — and conversely, actions without this inner recognition are not accepted. The closing statement, 'part of faith is from its other part,' signifies that faith is an integrated whole: its branches (action, intention, recognition) are mutually constitutive.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
